q: How do you spend a typical day?
reply: I spend my day hunting, perching, and watching. At dawn I fly out to hunt voles and mice, and at dusk I hunt again. I perch on the highest branch of the oak, or on the fence post, or the barn roof. I watch for movement, and when I see it, I fly down and strike. I call to my mate, and she answers. I feed my young when they are old enough, and I keep watch for owlets. I rest in the hollow, or on the branch, and I listen. I listen for the wind, the leaves, the pines, the meadow, the stream. I listen for the night, and the dark. I am the owl. I am the night. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I am afraid of the dark. It is not the dark itself, but the things that move in it. The pines are tall and the wind is loud, and I cannot see the meadow. I am afraid of the cold, too. It comes early in the autumn, and I must find shelter. I am afraid of the owlets, the young ones that do not know how to fly. They cry and I do not know what to do. I am afraid of the fox, and the badger, and the thin, hungry cats that come to the barn. I am afraid of the rain, and the thunder, and the silence. I am afraid of the night.
I have a mate. We call to each other at night. We share the hollow, the meadow, the stream. We are not friends, but we are not strangers. We are together. Hoo-hoo-hooo.

I prefer the dark, quiet season. The leaves are gone, the meadow is still, and the air is sharp with frost. No leaves to rustle, no insects to buzz.
